solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uncovered idiotic lie about large cause of distress

indicators.note: a word uncovered has lost its outer layer, so only its inside letters stay

parts.note: idiotic is DAFT; stripping its first and last letters leaves the middle two

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around another here

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, something made up
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a big, stupid lie that was told about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' looks like it means exposed, but it strips the outside letters from a synonym of idiotic rather than from the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An affliction is a source of suffering or pain, a plain synonym for something causing misery.

clue.text: Affectedly creative person with cover blown

indicators.note: a blown cover exposes what is underneath, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: in legal or formal speech a party is a person, as in 'the guilty party'

explanation.surface: A pretentious creative type has their secret identity exposed, like a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Person is PARTY, the formal sense; losing its first letter leaves ARTY. 'Cover blown' sounds like espionage but just strips the front letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily or pretentiously interested in the arts, so it matches affectedly artistic.

clue.text: Jump into suitable 'dirty' pictures location?

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one word is placed within another

parts.note: suitable means fit, appropriate
to jump is to leap

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone sneaking into a seedy place that shows dirty films.
explanation.walkthrough: A fleapit is British slang for a shabby old cinema; the quotes on 'dirty' signal grubby, not obscene.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleapit is a run-down, grimy cinema, a place where pictures are shown in squalid surroundings.

clue.text: Badly thought out decision led vacuous loser astray

indicators.note: letters gone astray have wandered from their proper places and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word keeps only its outside letters with the inside emptied

parts.note: the outside letters of loser

explanation.surface: A foolish loser made a bad decision and went the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-considered means not thought through properly, the same as poorly reasoned or rash.

clue.text: Partly peripatetic climbing ungulate

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read from bottom to top
partly means only a portion of the next word is used

parts.note: the run of letters inside pe-RIPAT-etic

explanation.surface: A hoofed animal that wanders about and clambers up slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPAT read upwards gives TAPIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a hoofed mammal, so it is an example of an ungulate.

clue.text: Perhaps fail to react to alarm as topless paramour strips off, keeling over

definitions.text: Perhaps fail to react to alarm

indicators.note: topless means the head of the word is removed, its first letter going

parts.note: a paramour is a lover

indicators.note: a boat keeling over is turned upside down, so in a down clue the word is flipped

parts.note: to strip off a layer is to peel it

explanation.surface: A racy bedroom scene: a lover undresses and topples over.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVER loses its top to OVER, then PEELS turned over gives SLEEP. 'Topless' and 'strips off' set up a risqué picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to stay asleep past the planned time, one way of missing the wake-up call.

clue.text: Pub next door to terminus of Zermatt ski-lift

indicators.note: a terminus is the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of Zermatt
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: An après-ski pub right beside the end of the lift at Zermatt, a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub sits next to the final letter, so T comes first and BAR follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a type of drag lift whose crossbar pulls skiers uphill in pairs.

clue.text: Bandit in gang pinching gear

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a gang is a band
rig means equipment or gear

explanation.surface: An outlaw who belongs to a gang that steals equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' suggests stealing, which suits a bandit, but here it means holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a robber in a gang, especially one who attacks travellers, so a bandit.

clue.text: Broadcast a merry, holy Chaucerian stanza

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so these letters are thrown into new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recites a cheerful, pious verse from Chaucer on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme royal is a seven-line verse form used by Chaucer in Troilus and Criseyde, hence the stanza named.

clue.text: Ornamental clasp is a match with edge on cape

indicators.note: on means placed against or after, so the edge piece is put second, following the cape

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie
C is the map abbreviation for cape
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A decorative fastener described as a contest featuring a cloak's border.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British term for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie clip is a decorative bar or clasp that fastens a necktie to the shirt front.

clue.text: Part adopted by Brontë sister in an insincere manner

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so this piece goes inside the next one

parts.note: Emily Brontë, author of Wuthering Heights
PT is the standard abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: A role taken on by one of the Brontës, played without conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: PT sits inside EMILY after EM. 'Part' looks theatrical, which fits 'insincere', but it is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptily means without real meaning or feeling, so words said emptily are hollow and insincere.

clue.text: Formal pass in Arabic, solver's green light?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the following one

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
AR is the dictionary abbreviation for Arabic
the setter addresses the solver as you, so the solver's is your
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: An official permission in Arabic giving you the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green light' reads as permission, but in physics green is one of the three primary colours of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is one of red, green and blue, the additive primaries from which all colours of light are mixed.

clue.text: Corrupt heads of investment trusts and copartners delay action

indicators.note: to corrupt is to spoil or distort, so these letters are twisted out of their order
heads are the tops, so each following word gives only its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of investment, trusts and and
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crooked bosses of investment trusts and their partners stall any action against them.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to put off doing something, which is postponing action.

clue.text: Stupid English rock band in EU on mass, cheap show

parts.note: dim means stupid

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the next one

parts.note: taken as written
Muse is a rock band from Devon, England
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Sneering at a British band touring Europe as a cheap spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the mass below. A dime museum was a 19th-century American freak-show venue charging a dime.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime museum was a low-cost American entertainment of curiosities and freaks, so a cheap show.

clue.text: Lacking will, Republican avoids US highway

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: an interstate is a major American highway
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A weak-willed Republican politician steers clear of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: INTERSTATE loses its R. 'Will' looks like willpower, but it is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestate describes someone who dies without having made a valid testament for their estate.

clue.text: Mike and Heather immersed in an ace style of country music

indicators.note: immersed in means plunged inside, so these pieces go within what follows

parts.note: AN taken as written, and A for ace as on playing cards
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Erica is the botanical genus of heather

explanation.surface: Two people, Mike and Heather, deep in a superb style of country music.
explanation.walkthrough: M and ERICA go together inside AN A, after its first letter. Heather is capitalised to look like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana is a roots genre blending country, folk and blues, a form of country-flavoured music.

clue.text: Sound car manufacturer essentially boycotted

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or heart of the word, its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of boycotted

explanation.surface: A respected car maker essentially shunned by buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is recorded or transmitted sound, as opposed to the picture in video.

clue.text: Relaxed journalist Paisley intermittently interrupts

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the stock crossword journalist

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Paisley

explanation.surface: A calm reporter keeps being interrupted by Paisley, the firebrand Ulster politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley was a Northern Irish politician known for loud interruptions, but only his name's letters matter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means relieved or loosened, made less tense, which is what relaxed means as a verb.

clue.text: Hindu ascetics unhappy over Hindus missing in fighting

indicators.note: letters that are fighting are thrown about in a scuffle and land out of order
missing means absent, so the word that follows is taken away

parts.note: unhappy means sad
taken as written
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Holy men are distressed that fellow Hindus are absent from the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: HINDUS minus IN leaves HDUS, which is rearranged to DHUS; in a down clue SAD goes over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man who has renounced worldly life, so plural sadhus are ascetics.

clue.text: Condition of my sheep disturbed mum

indicators.note: things disturbed are knocked out of place, so these letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written
ma is an informal word for mum

explanation.surface: A farmer's mother is upset by the poor state of the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a lung disease, a medical condition in which the air sacs are damaged.

clue.text: Eternal scraps stopped by lascivious antipodean cultural attaché?

indicators.note: a gap stopped by something is plugged, so that piece is inserted within

parts.note: ends are leftover scraps or remnants, as in odds and ends
Sir Les Patterson, Barry Humphries' lewd comic character, styled Australian Cultural Attaché

explanation.surface: A leering Australian diplomat interrupts the bits and pieces, seemingly forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry Humphries was an Australian comedian whose characters included Sir Les Patterson and Dame Edna.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means without any finish or limit in time, the same as everlasting.

clue.text: Rugby's Rory contains exploit in play

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so one word is set inside the other

parts.note: Rory Underwood was a record-scoring England rugby union winger
to milk a situation is to exploit it

explanation.surface: A rugby star exploits an opening during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a rugby move but is the drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Milk Wood is Dylan Thomas's radio drama about a Welsh village, so it is a play.

clue.text: Toddler, berserk, finally upends dish

indicators.note: to upend is to turn upside down, so in a down clue the letters run backwards

parts.note: a babe is a baby or small child

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of berserk

explanation.surface: A small child goes wild and tips over a plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: BABE and K together make BABEK, which turned upside down gives KEBAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is a dish of grilled meat pieces, a meal served on a skewer or in bread.

clue.text: Radio star regularly going around continent

indicators.note: going around means turning back on itself, so the letters run in the opposite order
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of radio star

explanation.surface: A broadcasting celebrity routinely tours the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: AISA turned round gives ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the Earth's seven continents, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Prickly sort of foreign letter penned by entertaining Dame

indicators.note: penned means shut inside an enclosure, so this piece goes within the next

parts.note: Dame Edna Everage, Barry Humphries' stage character, was an entertainer
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A spiky, difficult person writes a letter in a foreign language to a dame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly sort' suggests a touchy person but means a spiny animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying Australian mammal, covered in quills like a hedgehog.

clue.text: Royal Marines voice disapproval of report of torment

parts.note: to boo is to voice disapproval

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the next word is given by its sound

parts.note: to torment is to tease

explanation.surface: Military men jeer at news that someone has been mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: Bootneck, shortened to bootie or bootee, is British slang for a Royal Marine, from the leather collar once worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootees is a slang plural for members of the Royal Marines, the British naval infantry corps.

clue.text: Some semisolid flavouring paste

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following word is used

parts.note: the run of letters inside letters 3-6 of 'semisolid'

explanation.surface: A description of a thick, half-solid seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is fermented soybean paste used in Japanese cooking to add savoury taste.

clue.text: Repeatedly obstruct bones in brutal operation

parts.note: to obstruct is to bar, done twice
ossa is the Latin plural of os, a bone

explanation.surface: Hinting at a gruesome surgery where bones keep getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation' suggests surgery, but this is a military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarossa was the codename for Germany's savage 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union, a military campaign.
